Overclaim: FMT works because C. scindens restores secondary bile acids in patients.
SupportedClaim: Donor FMT and a purified spore product reduce recurrent-CDI risk in their trial populations; C. scindens has bile-acid-dependent effects in specified experimental systems.
WhyDowngraded: Intervention bundle and single-strain mechanism come from different estimands.

Overclaim: Donor strains engrafted, therefore those strains caused the cure.
SupportedClaim: Shotgun strain tracking establishes donor-origin persistence after FMT; a mediator effect on cure requires an additional identified design.
WhyDowngraded: Post-treatment association can reflect treatment delivery, host selection, or outcome-related survival.

Overclaim: F. nucleatum causes human colorectal cancer.
SupportedClaim: F. nucleatum is reproducibly associated with human CRC and can promote CRC phenotypes in specified mouse, cell, and xenograft systems.
WhyDowngraded: No randomized targeted human intervention establishes prevention or treatment benefit.

Overclaim: A significant mediation or MR result proves a microbial treatment will work.
SupportedClaim: Mediation and MR provide design-specific causal bridges under explicit assumptions; their estimands need not equal a short-term microbial intervention effect.
WhyDowngraded: Unmeasured mediator-outcome confounding and horizontal pleiotropy remain design-specific threats.

Overclaim: Mouse FMT reproduced the phenotype, so the same mechanism operates in people.
SupportedClaim: Host-transfer experiments establish sufficiency in that model and intervention context; human transport requires matched exposure, outcome, ecology, and dose.
WhyDowngraded: Species, diet, housing, immune state, and donor-recipient compatibility can modify the effect.
